title: Neoliberal Doxa across the World-System: Economic Beliefs in the Global North and South
description: How taken-for-granted economic beliefs vary across core and peripheral positions in the world-system.

title: Not All Moves Are Equal: How Employment and Capital Composition Shape Residential Mobility Strategies
description: Why households with different employment situations and forms of capital pursue different residential mobility strategies.

title: The Moral Economies of Influencer Culture: Visibility, Value, and Intersectional Precarity
description: How visibility is converted into economic value in the influencer economy, and how that conversion reproduces intersectional forms of precarity.

title: Divergent Value Trajectories: Cultural and Economic Liberalization in the United States, 2004–2024
description: Two decades of survey evidence on whether cultural and economic attitudes have liberalized together or pulled apart.

title: Platform Labor, Identity, and Inequality: A Systematic Review of Gig Work Through an Intersectional Lens
description: A systematic review synthesizing what the gig-work literature shows — and overlooks — about identity and inequality on labor platforms.

title: Social Capital and the Geography of Opportunity: Economic Connectedness, Bias, and Mobility in the United States
description: How cross-class social connectedness and social bias shape economic mobility across U.S. places.

title: Item Level Bias in the NSF-sponsored Science Knowledge Scale, 2006–2024
authors: J. Micah Roos, Waris Ahmad Faizi, and Shih-Hao Lin
description: Measurement work on differential item functioning in the science-knowledge scale used across two decades of national surveys.
